notes:
POC objective: validate Dedicated capacity meets SLA targets for live fleet assistant and high-throughput reranking pipeline. Short summary bullets:
- Primary workload: hybrid real-time chat for drivers (low latency, p99 <250ms per response) + asynchronous reranking for route suggestions (throughput focus).
- Model preference: prefer Redwood-verified Llama-2-70B-quant (int8/awq) for quality; fallback path to 13B quantized variant for burst/low-cost mode.
- Capacity ask: initial reserved pool projected 8 x A100-80GB equiv (estimate) to meet target throughput; planning exercise to map to Redwood SKUs.
- Performance targets agreed in discovery: end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latencies for chat under production trace: <60ms / <140ms / <260ms, token generation steady-state. Reranking: sustain 2k QPS (small inputs) with p95 <300ms.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — willingness to commit to annual reserved if unit economics within 20% of current self-hosted infra TCO.
- POC test plan (runbook):
  * Warm-up: 6-hour gradual ramp to steady concurrency to prime KV cache and batching.
  * Load tests: stepped ramp to target QPS (50%, 75%, 100%, 130%) across representative prompt mix.
  * Soak tests: 72-hour continuous load at 95% target to check memory leaks, GPU thermal throttling, backpressure handling.
  * Failure injection: simulate instance loss + model-fallback routing to confirm graceful degradation and SLA alignment.
  * Workload fidelity: use recorded driver dialogs (anonymized), route candidate batches, and synthetic adversarial prompts to measure quality regressions.
- Observability & metrics: need token-level cost, per-GPU utilization, batch sizes distribution, KV cache hit rate, and tail latency (p99/p999). Redwood Console dashboard request made (link above).
- Early lab results (internal Redwood-run):
  * 2026-03-04 internal load: 6 x A100-equivalent sustained reranking at 1.6k QPS p95 280ms; CPU host network pinned at 85%.
  * 2026-03-06 warmup soak (24h): identified KV cache warmup pattern — first 2 hours saw 30% higher latency; recommended pre-warm strategy and persistent prefix cache.
  * 2026-03-08 failure injection: failover to 13B quant worked but increased p99 by ~120ms; acceptable as documented fallback SLA.
- Security/compliance notes: Harborline requires SSO SAML + org-level audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance. Data residency: primary in US East; backups archived 90 days. HSM/KMS key escrow review in progress.
- Procurement/contract: Harborline legal wants explicit credits for downtime >0.5% monthly and strict definitions for 'throughput guarantee' measured as sustained QPS over 30-minute windows.
- Quote request: provide two reserved sizing options: Conservative (6 x A100 equiv, auto-burst to 8) and Performance (10 x A100 equiv with dedicated throughput windows). Include migration & private deployment add-on pricing.
- Recent activity timeline:
  * 2026-02-22 discovery call (Elena, Diego) — collected sample prompts and fleet latency histograms.
  * 2026-02-27 security deep-dive (Priya + Harborline SecOps) — SSO/KMS checklist delivered (drive link).
  * 2026-03-04 Redwood internal benchmark run (see notes).

  * 2026-03-08 live failover test with Harborline infra team — Fireflies ff-7901221.
  * 2026-03-09 pricing & SLA draft sent (gmail thread).
- Quotes on blockers/risks: network egress limits on their on-prem site could throttle throughput; firewall team requested specific IP ranges and 3-day maintenance window for testing. Legal open item on SLA credit calculus and force majeure language.
- Next steps (short): finalize reserved SKU mapping w/Infra (by 2026-03-12), deliver two final pricing options + SLA markup (by 2026-03-15), schedule exec review with Harborline CTO (proposed 2026-03-18).
